Pope, In sandy soil, when deep you delve, you reach the springs below; / The more you learn, the freer streams of wisdom flow, against Shuddhananda Bharati's quite different As deep you dig the sand spring flows; a third presentation, the agaram-thirukkural transcription of 396, carries the same two lines, so the wording is not one site's drift. The locator is right: kurals 391 to 400 are chapter 40, and the chapter is Kalvi, which Pope and Drew both head Learning (thirukkural.io labels it Education, the same chapter). It sits in Book II, as the evidence says, since Book I ends at chapter 38. The translation credit is right: Pope's complete English Kural is The Sacred Kurral of Tiruvalluva-Nayanar, W. H. Allen, London, 1886. Tiruvalluvar is not banned, not at cap, not shipped, and opens like nothing shipped (shipped.js clean). The break after below; is the couplet's own; both line heads keep their capitals; the quotation ends in a full stop; no straight double quote; no dash in the source; the source leads with the name and runs 84 characters; Poetry is the form of a didactic couplet; the subject is learning, which is the month's own ground. Second, Pope's title calls the Kural sacred and Tamil tradition calls it the Tamil Veda, so an owner could read it against the scripture exclusion; it is secular ethical verse by a named poet, not liturgy, so I would let it stand.
